summary.text: Schist is a medium-grained metamorphic rock, usually formed from fine-grained sedimentary rock such as shale.
It is rich in platy minerals like mica, lined up so that the rock splits easily into thin flakes or plates, a property called schistosity.
It typically forms at a medium grade of metamorphism during mountain building, when rock is squeezed harder in one direction than in others.

facts.label: Engineering trouble
facts.value: Bedrock with pronounced planes of weakness

facts.label: Oversized crystals
facts.value: Often garnet, staurolite, kyanite, sillimanite or cordierite

items.prompt: A mudstone is metamorphosed more and more strongly over time. In what order does it change?
items.explain: Mudstone first becomes slate, then phyllite, then mica schist, and further metamorphism turns the schist into gneiss.

items.prompt: Why can schist be peeled apart into thin flakes so easily?

options.label: Its flat mineral grains are aligned
It is full of gas bubbles
Its grains are too tiny to bond

items.explain: Platy minerals such as mica are strongly oriented in one direction, and the rock splits along these aligned grains.

items.prompt: A rock with almost no mica or other platy minerals goes through medium-grade metamorphism. Why is it unlikely to become a strongly flaky schist?

options.label: Easy splitting needs plenty of platy minerals
Only igneous rock can turn into schist
Its grains grow too large to see

items.explain: Schistosity normally develops only when the rock contains abundant platy minerals, so its composition must allow them to form.

items.prompt: Mica schist is heated and squeezed even further. Why does it lose much of its easy splitting?

options.label: It melts and cools as glass
Water fills and seals its layers

items.explain: Dehydration reactions convert platy minerals into granular ones such as feldspar, reducing schistosity and turning the rock into gneiss.

items.prompt: Graphite schist is uncommon. What must its parent sedimentary beds have been rich in?
items.explain: Graphite schist can form from metamorphism of sedimentary beds containing abundant organic carbon.

items.prompt: Engineers learn that a building site sits on schist bedrock. What is their main worry?

options.label: It has marked planes of weakness
It is too hard to dig into

items.explain: Schist bedrock can challenge civil engineering because of its pronounced planes of weakness.
